subject: Dedicated capacity sizing proposal and SKU allocation for OrbisLabs pilot
messages:
From: Alexa Munroe <alexa@orbislabs.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for OrbisLabs pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the routing/fallback examples. We're starting to plan the dedicated-capacity pilot (internal name: "Orbis Pilot") and need guidance on SKU selection. High level:

- Workload mix: long-context summarization (average 15–30k tokens), embeddings for search (dense, small payloads), and high-concurrency text generation (many short chats).
- Peak: ~200 requests/sec across regions, with spiky bursts up to 380 RPS for short gen calls.
- Latency SLO: 150ms p50 for short gen, 400ms p95 for long-context summarization.
- Memory/KV cache: summarization uses large KV cache per session (hosted state), estimated working set ~60–90GB per model instance.
- Timeline: want pilot up in June, then reserve committed capacity if results match.
- Budget: aiming for predictable reserved unit economics; procurement is involved (cc'd).

Can you recommend a SKU allocation (H100 / A100 / L4) and a minimal reserved footprint for the pilot? Also any suggestions on fallbacks, tiling, or model variants we should plan for? I've attached a compact workload profile export.

Thanks,
Alexa Munroe
Head of ML Engineering, OrbisLabs
attachments: orbis_workload_profile.csv

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alexa Munroe <alexa@orbislabs.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbislabs.ai
Date: 2026-04-26T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for OrbisLabs pilot

Hi Alexa — great to see the profile, this helps a lot. Quick read and initial proposal below; we should do a 45-min ops deep-dive next week to validate traffic shapes and token distributions.

High-level recommendation (pilot-ready):
- Hybrid allocation: L4-heavy for embeddings and low-memory gen; H100 for the long-context summarization model; A100 as a fall-through for mid-memory, high-throughput backstop.
- Pilot minimum: 6 L4 slots + 4 H100 slots + 2 A100 slots. That maps to the expected concurrency and gives headroom for bursts using smart routing.
- Rationale in one line: L4 = best tokens/$ for short stateless workloads and embeddings; H100 = large HBM & fp8 throughput for long-context KV-heavy summarization; A100 = compatibility fallback for models that don't quantize as well and for cost-optimized batching.

Operational notes / immediate asks:
- We will enable prefix/KV caching and per-customer routing policies to reduce H100 active memory pressure.
- Plan to deploy model variants: quantized long-context on H100, non-quantized or fp16 fallback on A100, and trimmed low-memory gen on L4.
- Please share a 24h sample of RPS by endpoint and percentiles for token lengths (esp. how often 30k+ tokens occur).

I've attached an initial SKU allocation spreadsheet with per-slot throughput estimates and a placeholder pricing delta. After the ops call we'll firm up numbers and draft a reserve term sheet.

Next step: are you available Wed 5/1 10:00–11:00 PT for an ops deep-dive?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: kimberly_initial_sku_proposal.xlsx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-26T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Orbis pilot — technical sizing rationale and fallthrough plan

Rishi / Dev — looping you in for technical sizing before I present to the customer. Quick notes and numbers I want us to validate:

Context (from Alexa's profile):
- Long-context summarization workload dominates memory (60–90GB working set per active session).
- Embeddings are high QPS but low memory per request.
- Short gen calls are latency-sensitive; they drive p50 SLA.

Proposed pilot slots (6 L4 / 4 H100 / 2 A100) — cost and perf tradeoffs:
- H100 (4 slots):
  - Pros: >2x throughput for fp8 quantized long-context compared to A100; 80–120GB HBM across multiple instances depending on node type; ideal for very large KV caches and long context state.
  - Cons: higher unit cost; more sensitive to kernel availability for rare ops.
- A100 (2 slots):
  - Pros: Proven ecosystem compatibility, strong fp16 perf, predictable memory (40–80GB depending on variant). Good as fallback when quantization regresses.
  - Cons: Higher tokens/$ than L4 for short stateless workloads; lower HBM than H100 variants we recommend.
- L4 (6 slots):
  - Pros: Lowest tokens/$ for embeddings and small-context generation; great for streaming responses and model shards that fit in smaller memory.
  - Cons: Limited HBM (not suitable for 30k-token working sets).

Operational mitigations to reduce H100 pressure:
- Aggressive prefix/KV cache eviction policies and cached summarization checkpoints for sessions with repeated access patterns.
- Request steering: send short calls to L4; long-context to H100. If H100 capacity saturated, A100 can accept queued requests with slightly higher latency.
- Quantization acceptance tests during rollout (A/B on small traffic).

Throughput math (rough):
- Embeddings: L4 slot ~1200 emb/sec; need 2–3 slots for steady-state 200 RPS embedding traffic (batching will help).
- Short gen: L4 slot ~80 tok/sec for small models; with 6 slots we cover p50 targets and reduce cost.
- Long-context summarization: H100 slot ~10–20 tok/sec for dense 30k contexts (depends on model); 4 slots provide headroom for a handful of concurrent long sessions.

Questions for both of you:
1) Are my HBM assumptions correct for the H100 node types we offer in Dedicated (GPU+40GB?). If we need 100GB per instance we should define exact node SKUs.
2) Do we have a reservation-pack that mixes L4/H100 on the same term (discount math)? If not, we'll need to draft a blended term sheet.

I'll incorporate your feedback and send a customer-ready SKU + price proposal.

—Kim

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-26T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Orbis pilot — technical sizing rationale and fallthrough plan

Thanks Kim — good summary. Agreed with the hybrid approach and a slightly smaller H100 footprint for pilot to reduce initial cost while still validating long-context behavior. Final internal recommendation to present to Orbis: 

- Pilot allocation to propose: 6 L4 slots, 4 H100 slots, 2 A100 slots (same as your ask) but we should offer an optional scaled-back pilot: 4 L4 / 3 H100 / 2 A100 if Orbis wants a lower starting price.
- Commit recommendation: 12-month reserved block with 3-month pilot conversion credit; include a cross-SKU blended discount model (we can price L4 at standard reservation rate, H100 at a higher tier, and apply an overall blended discount to the deal).
- Fallthrough policy to include in SOW: route to L4 for short gen and embeddings; route to H100 for long-context; if H100 saturation >85% route to A100 and queue with soft-SLA warning.

Action items:
- Kimberly: send the pilot proposal to Alexa with both the full and scaled-back options, include the blended pricing sheet and a DocuSign link for pilot reserve (see link).
- Dev: confirm per-slot HBM numbers for the H100 node types we can ship in Dedicated and confirm whether we can bundle H100+L4 into a single reserve.

I'll be on the customer call if needed.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product Sales, Redwood Inference
